name: Alcântara Space Center
tagline: Brazil's equatorial launch centre: VLS-1 failures, the 2003 pad explosion, sounding rockets
description: Alcântara, on Brazil's northern coast in Maranhão at 2.3 degrees south, is among the launch sites closest to the equator. Construction began in 1982, and the Brazilian Air Force runs it for the Brazilian Space Agency. The first launch was a Sonda 2 sounding rocket on 21 February 1990. Brazil's VLS-1 satellite launcher failed on both flights, on 2 November 1997 and 11 December 1999. On 22 August 2003 the third VLS-1 exploded on its pad two days before launch and killed 21 people. No orbital launch from Alcântara has yet succeeded: Innospace's Hanbit-Nano failed in December 2025. Sounding rockets and test vehicles keep flying, a 2019 agreement with the United States covers foreign launches, and the site was built on land from which over 300 families were moved in 1980.
